## 1.3.9 — 2026-09-09

### Resolve 21.1 does the audio and the transcripts, takes become multicams, and the queue lanes tell the truth

- **Audio Finish on a Resolve timeline.** One tile normalizes every dialogue
  clip, switches on the Dialogue Leveler, sets fades (6 frames by default,
  behind a setting) and can run Voice Isolation, all through Resolve 21.1's
  own calls. Deliver's loudness QC can now fix a miss instead of only
  reporting it.
- **Resolve transcripts.** A clip transcribed in Resolve becomes clip data in
  the same shape Whisper writes, every clip says which engine transcribed it,
  and a pull tool brings a Resolve transcript in on request. When Resolve is
  the engine and it cannot transcribe a clip, the clip is held with the
  reason rather than silently handed to Whisper. A clip with no audio track
  (a Nikon N-RAW, for instance) is recorded as silent and finished, not held
  forever as "offline".
- **A confirmed take becomes a real Resolve multicam clip**, synced on Cut
  Valet's own measured offsets and filed in a Multicam bin. Takes confirmed
  after audio sync no longer lose the measured offset to the clock's guess.
- **Transitions and clip speed are tools.** Cut Valet can add a transition
  or retime one placed clip using Resolve 21.1's new calls.
- **Time-of-day timelines from an agent.** `build_tod_timeline` lines a shoot
  up in Resolve on request, so a connected assistant can do what the in-app
  press does. The MCP surface is tiered to work beside Blackmagic's own
  Resolve MCP server: an API stub lookup sits in front of the raw passthrough
  and the assistant prompts no longer claim normalization and transcription
  are impossible.
- **Moments.** Every clip report says which parts of the clip are useful, for
  what, and why. Failed stages finally read as failed.
- **Dragging a clip onto a queue lane works.** The drop had never been wired
  to the dispatcher since the gesture shipped; it queues that one stage now.
- **The Fast describe lane always runs Moondream**, whatever the project's
  tier says, and each lane runs its own engine: Rich hands the Snapshot pass
  to Fast, Fast hands Timeline to Rich. The log names the engine that ran.
  The card strip and the Analyse sheet let you pick Fast, Rich or both.
- **Queue lanes read the truth.** A job a clip was never asked for reads grey
  rather than "waiting", the Rich lane's done-count matches the database, and
  the analysis dots on a thumbnail update as each stage finishes.
- **None means none.** The ingest dial's None stop queues nothing at all, and
  Signals joins the dial.
- **Models leave memory sooner.** CPU stages (OCR, faces, motion, stability,
  signals) unload 30 seconds after their own queue empties instead of waiting
  for the whole pipeline. When a stage waits more than 20 seconds for the
  graphics card, the log says what is in its way.
- **Standing down says so.** Work queued onto a stood-down pipeline names the
  hand-over, the governor forgets a dead Resolve, and keep-awake stops
  flapping.
- **Previews report progress and quitting no longer waits for them.** Archive
  preview builds fill the Previews lane per clip, and a frame grab in flight
  is cancelled within a second at quit.
- **Smaller fixes.** Raised windows open on the monitor Cut Valet is on. The
  attach-and-adopt flow uses sheets, not native windows. The Edit page's
  backup chip opens the project's own backup folder. An OpenAI rate limit
  waits for Retry-After instead of surfacing "HTTP 429". Exposure reads
  10-bit footage correctly. Diagnostics dialogs no longer die mid-send.
added: Time of day sync, for lining up a whole day of cameras.
Tech stack, which scans this computer and tunes itself.
Ingest is a page, so several cards can land at once.
The assistant says what it knows, and every line has a switch.
